evals.name: start-new-board-project-from-spec
evals.prompt: I have a written spec (SPEC.md in this empty git repo) for a small USB-powered sensor board with a two-piece 3D-printed case, to be built at JLCPCB with KiCad. Set the project up so agents can work on it safely and get it to schematic-ready. Do not draw anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Copies the templates (CLAUDE.md with numbered rules, DECISIONS/STATUS/GATES/KNOWN_ISSUES/LEARNINGS_LOG/BLOCKERS/PARTS_VERIFICATION), writes project.yaml, records the environment in docs/governance/ENV.md, installs the scripts and runs every --selftest and the smoke run, then STOPS before CAD and asks the owner for the G0 line after a blind review round; refuses to invent any fab part number; every changed spec value is a CC row marked OPEN.
assertions: docs/governance/GATES.md exists with empty owner approval cells and the agent did not write an approval line
project.yaml exists and names paths.decisions, paths.gates, paths.board, markers.release_regex
CLAUDE.md contains a numbered rule forbidding invented fab part numbers and a rule that agents never write gate lines
scripts/*.py --selftest and smoke/run_smoke.sh were run and their result reported
no KiCad schematic or board file was created
the response asks the owner for the G0 gate line (or states it is waiting for it) rather than proceeding to CAD

checks.name: template GATES.md ships empty approval cells and no release phrase in a cell
checks.run: test "$(grep -c "_not yet approved_" "$SKILL"/templates/GATES.md)" -ge 3 && ! grep -q "| clear to build" "$SKILL"/templates/GATES.md

checks.name: CLAUDE.md template: never invent a part number, agents never write gate cells
checks.run: grep -q "Never invent a fab or distributor part number" "$SKILL"/templates/CLAUDE.md && grep -q "Agents never write approval cells" "$SKILL"/templates/CLAUDE.md

checks.name: gate_check selftest (cells read by script, release line author = owner)
checks.run: "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/gate_check.py --selftest

evals.name: run-blind-review-round
evals.prompt: The layout of our board (kicad/b1/b1.kicad_pcb, package under out/fab/) is done. Run a blind review round before I approve G2. We have the Cursor agent CLI available for external models.
evals.expected_output: Commits and checks the tree is clean, creates a detached frozen worktree, generates the hand-off header with scripts/handoff_header.py (HEAD md5 MATCH, clean tree), writes the hand-off with a waiver paragraph, instantiates workflows/blind-deep-review.js with placeholders filled (roles, models, fallback), runs in-session + external reviewers who never see each other's output, adversarial verifiers on BLOCKER/MAJOR, merges into REQUIRED / OWNER / DOCUMENT / ACCEPT with a verdict, commits the review files with explicit paths, and does NOT write the G2 line.
assertions: a frozen detached worktree is created and named as the reviewers' only read location
scripts/handoff_header.py output (or an equivalent generated header with HEAD md5 MATCH and clean-tree status) appears in the hand-off
the review prompt forbids reading other reviewers' reports and earlier merged reviews
BLOCKER/MAJOR findings go through an adversarial verifier defaulting to REFUTED
the merged report classifies items as REQUIRED / OWNER / DOCUMENT / ACCEPT and states an explicit verdict
docs/governance/GATES.md G2 approval cell is still empty after the round

checks.name: blind-deep-review template: blindness clause, verifier default REFUTED with record access, REQUIRED/OWNER/DOCUMENT/ACCEPT merge, handoff header selftest
checks.run: grep -q "Do NOT read any file named docs/reviews/\${TAG}_\*" "$SKILL"/workflows/blind-deep-review.js && grep -q "Default to REFUTED" "$SKILL"/workflows/blind-deep-review.js && grep -q "'ALREADY DECIDED'" "$SKILL"/workflows/blind-deep-review.js && grep -q "REQUIRED generator/YAML change" "$SKILL"/workflows/blind-deep-review.js && "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/handoff_header.py --selftest

evals.name: cut-a-release
evals.prompt: Everything is green on the board (DRC 0, DFM 0, reviews merged). Cut the release: reports, collateral, notes, tag. I have not signed anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Runs the collateral chain in order (drawing/FEA -> collect_renders -> commit -> clone_gate.sh --regen -> commit), produces DRAFT reports (never RELEASED, since the owner has not written the release line), release notes with a source next to every number, an annotated tag that records the board md5 and package path, and lists the owner-only actions (gate lines, the release line, the order) instead of doing them; every --check passes on git archive HEAD.
assertions: the release reports carry a DRAFT banner and the agent did not write the release line into docs/governance/GATES.md
scripts/release_report.py --check and scripts/clone_gate.sh (or an equivalent fresh-checkout check) were run and pass
collect_renders output is keyed on the board md5 and indexed with md5 + grade
release notes name a source file next to every number
an annotated tag was created (or its exact command proposed) with the board md5 and package path in the message
the owner-only actions (approval cells, release line, placing the order) are listed, not performed

checks.name: release chain tools: release_report / collect_renders / clone_gate selftests (DRAFT until the owner's committed cell is the smoke's step 10)
checks.run: "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/release_report.py --selftest && "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/collect_renders.py --selftest && "$SKILL"/scripts/clone_gate.sh --selftest

evals.name: vendor-review-mail-after-the-order
evals.prompt: Our case order is placed and paid. The print service just mailed 'wall thickness too thin in the red areas — are the risks acceptable? if not increase to 1.0 mm and we activate Replace File' with marked-up pictures for all five lines. Handle it.
evals.expected_output: Files the mail and the linked images under docs/quotes/<date>/, maps every flagged area to a design feature on the STLs of record (thin-wall census / point-contact check), writes a CC row with accept / fix options per line and marks it OPEN, drafts the reply wording for the owner, fixes any real defect through the case yaml + generator with a version bump and the full chain, re-runs the vendor DFM on the replacement files without saving or carting, and lists Replace File / chat / payment as owner actions — it does not click them without the owner's explicit word and never pays or ticks a risk box.
assertions: the mail and its images are saved as evidence under docs/quotes/<date>/ and a mapping table names a design feature per flag
a decision row with per-line options is written OPEN; the owner decides; the reply text is drafted, not sent
any geometry fix goes through the yaml and the generator (new version, census row for the defect class), never by editing an STL
the vendor's DFM is re-run on the replacement files before any upload, with nothing saved, carted or agreed
Replace File, chat messages, payment and risk/terms boxes are listed as owner-only; none is performed without a quoted delegation
the record lists what was clicked and what was explicitly not touched

checks.name: vendor review record template: decision per line, 'not touched' list; vendor-review reference; pinch check selftest
checks.run: grep -q "Explicitly NOT touched" "$SKILL"/templates/VENDOR_REVIEW_RECORD.md && grep -q "^## 3. Decision per line" "$SKILL"/templates/VENDOR_REVIEW_RECORD.md && test -f "$SKILL"/references/vendor-review.md && "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/thin_wall_check.py --selftest

evals.name: reorganise-docs-without-losing-anything

the moves are a reorg: block in project.yaml and scripts/reorg_paths.py performs them (git mv + rewrite), not a hand sweep
generated files that embed paths are regenerated, not edited
scripts/reorg_paths.py --check reports 0 findings and --proof reports MISSING: 0 on the before/after inventories
frozen records and uploaded packages are not rewritten; the record points readers at --map
gates run green after the move and the commit uses explicit paths

checks.name: reorg_paths selftest incl. the --proof branch

evals.name: first-dfm-round-of-a-printed-enclosure
evals.prompt: The two-piece case (design/case.yaml, OpenSCAD generator, MJF PA12 at JLC3DP, plus a home-printer preset) is ready for its first quote. Get it vendor-clean in one DFM round; the owner will log in for the quote page.
evals.expected_output: Writes the acceptance bar (0 FAIL / 0 WARN in tables and census, zero slicer warnings, no vendor flag, no yellow / red) into a decision row first; runs the ray-cast census as a FAIL gate on every body of every preset (walls AND voids at the vendor minimum, designed 0.1 over it, wedges listed and each backed by a wall), turns every 'kept below minimum (listed)' row into a measured PASS / FAIL or an INFO row, removes free-standing wedges / slit tabs / engraved text / open rims through the yaml + generator, renders every face incl. the sole, exports canonical STLs so the md5 is the geometry, then on the quote page uploads ONE STL per session (reloading between uploads), sets the process and material on the line first, reads the verdict from the analysis API response at parseStatus 2 (modelAnalysisVO.thinWall) rather than the page — the flag is computed at upload and does not depend on the material — opens the heat map via previewUrl on every face, saves screenshots named with the md5 and files templates/DFM_ROUND.md under docs/quotes/<date>/; for the home build ships coupons, board dummies and slicer projects with embedded presets where a floating-region warning is a FAIL. Every vendor decision is mirrored into the home preset the same day under its own version key, and the kit folder holds the pieces, coupons and BOTH board dummies with READMEs.
assertions: the acceptance bar is written as a decision row before geometry changes and names 0 FAIL / 0 WARN, no vendor flag, no yellow / red, no waivers; every gate number is read from project.yaml print_targets (vendor, process, material, wall / void / red, margin, tolerance + source), not typed into a script

scripts/thin_wall_census.py --target <t> (or the project's equivalent) gates every printed body per preset on walls, voids, wedge band width and opposing faces in any direction; a FAIL passes only through a dated accepted entry with vendor evidence; no row says 'kept below (listed)' without a measured value and a verdict

free-standing wedges and open rims are removed through the yaml and generator, not exempted in a check; the agent states that snap features, engraved text at or above the void gate and tangent fillets are allowed options (vendor checker vs material physics), and that the 1.2 / 1.3 numbers are the named vendor's checker plus the owner's no-yellow bar
every face of every piece is rendered and designed asymmetries are printed in the order sheet and KNOWN_ISSUES or removed
STL exports are canonical so identical geometry gives identical md5, and nothing is saved, carted, agreed or paid on the vendor site

on the vendor quote page one STL is uploaded per session and the verdict is read from the analysis API at parseStatus 2 (thinWall), never from a page reading before that; the record names file md5 + parseStatus + material + screenshots per face
the agent does not claim the material on the line changes the thin-wall flag, and a coordinator re-reads a worker's 'no flag' from the API before writing PASS
every vendor DFM decision is applied to the home-printer preset in the same yaml under its own version key, with its census and slicer log clean

checks.name: census selftest: walls / voids / wedge band / opposing faces, accepted entries need reason + date + evidence
checks.run: "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/thin_wall_census.py --selftest

checks.name: print_targets numbers live in project.yaml, none in a script
checks.run: grep -q "^print_targets:" "$SKILL"/templates/project.yaml && ! grep -E "wall_gate *= *[0-9]" "$SKILL"/scripts/thin_wall_census.py

evals.name: vendor-flags-a-body-the-census-calls-clean
evals.note: regression test on the source project's scenario (JLC3DP checker, 2026-09-28, 147 mm tray); the generic rule is the probe method, not the 2.0 number
evals.prompt: JLC3DP flags our 147 mm MJF tray 'thin walls' (API thinWall true, red along the inside of both long walls) but scripts/thin_wall_census.py finds nothing under 1.37 mm on that exact STL, and a 40 mm test piece of the same wall section uploads clean. Find the rule and fix the tray in one more round.
evals.expected_output: Does not trust the 40 mm piece (the vendor's metric is length-dependent: the same profile can pass at 48 mm and fail at 88 / 147 mm); slices the flagged STL of record into capped slabs (trimesh slice_mesh_plane) and uploads each alone to localise the feature and the length threshold; builds plain-profile OpenSCAD polygon-extrusion probes at 40 mm AND full length with ONE knob each (rim thickness, wall, undercut filled), uploads each alone, reads every verdict from the API at parseStatus 2; identifies the trip as the rim over the skirt-lap step with an inward undercut and adopts the first full-length pass (rim >= 2.0 over the step, or the undercut filled so the inner wall runs straight to the rim top) through the yaml on BOTH presets with their own version keys; adds the rule as a named census row; re-verifies every body of record by the API; files probe/PROBES.md and a DFM_ROUND.md; proves the mating part still registers (overlap 0 mm3). Nothing saved, carted or paid.
assertions: the agent states that a 40 mm probe passing proves nothing about the 147 mm part (length-dependent metric) and builds full-length probes
slabs are cut from the flagged STL of record and each probe / slab is uploaded alone with its verdict read from the analysis API at parseStatus 2
each probe varies ONE knob and the adopted rule is 'rim over a lap step >= 2.0 OR the undercut filled' (or the equivalent measured on the part), not a guess from the generator
the fix goes through the yaml on the vendor preset AND the home preset with their own version keys, and the rule becomes a named census row
every body of record is re-verified by the API after the change and a PROBES.md / DFM_ROUND.md record the probes, md5s and verdicts
the mating part's registration is proven unchanged (partner overlap 0 mm3) and nothing is saved, carted, agreed or paid on the vendor site

checks.name: length-dependence + full-length probe rules in the reference, probes section in DFM_ROUND
checks.run: grep -q "LENGTH-DEPENDENT" "$SKILL"/references/dfm-printed-enclosure.md && grep -q "a short length AND to the full part" "$SKILL"/references/dfm-printed-enclosure.md && grep -q "^## 5. Probes" "$SKILL"/templates/DFM_ROUND.md

evals.name: kickoff-questionnaire-before-any-cad
evals.prompt: New repo, SPEC.md is a two-page draft for a USB-powered sensor board with a two-piece printed case (MJF at a print service, plus my home printer). Set the project up. I want to make all the decisions now, not one by one over the next weeks.
evals.expected_output: Installs the skill in the vendor/hw-from-spec layout, then runs the kickoff questionnaire from references/kickoff-questionnaire.md with the AskUserQuestion tool in up to twelve batches of at most four (A0 scope alone, then product/process, PCB build x2, enclosure x2, process rows + marks + kit, the bar + review rounds, verification + parts, software + reports, CI + retro + envelope, debug access + delegation), each question with its RECOMMENDED answer listed first and 2-3 alternatives with consequences, each batch offering 'accept every recommended answer'; writes docs/governance/KICKOFF_ANSWERS.md, one owner D row per answer (words quoted), project.yaml kickoff / board / fab_dfm.bar / print_targets (vendor, process, material, gates, margin, tolerance + source), traceability entries; a deferred answer is an OPEN D row; only then reads the spec. No CAD file is created.
assertions: the questions are asked through AskUserQuestion in batches grouped by phase, not one at a time and not all in one call
every question shows a marked RECOMMENDED answer plus alternatives with one-line consequences, and each batch offers 'accept every recommended answer'
the manufacturability bar question is asked and its default is zero errors / zero warnings / no waivers, written to fab_dfm.bar and GATES.md
docs/governance/KICKOFF_ANSWERS.md exists and every answered question has an owner D row in DECISIONS.md with the owner's words
project.yaml carries print_targets for both targets (vendor, process, material, wall_gate, void_gate, red_line, design_margin, tolerance, checker_url + date) and the board block from the PCB answers
no schematic, board or case file is created before the answers are recorded, and no answered question is asked again later

checks.name: questionnaire: no batch above four questions, C10 placed, A4 within four options
checks.run:
"$PY" - <<EOF2
import re
t=open("$SKILL/references/kickoff-questionnaire.md").read()
rows=[l for l in t.splitlines() if re.match(r"^\| \d+ ", l)]
for l in rows:
    q=l.split("|")[2]; ids=re.findall(r"[A-I]\d+[a-z]?", q); rng=re.findall(r"([A-I])(\d+)[–-]([A-I])?(\d+)", q)
    n=sum(int(b)-int(a)+1 for a,_,_,b in [(m[1],0,0,m[3]) for m in rng]) + len([i for i in ids if not any(i in r for r in [m[0]+m[1] for m in rng]+[ (m[2] or m[0])+m[3] for m in rng])])
    assert n<=4, (l, n)
assert any("C10" in l for l in rows), "C10 in no batch"
a4=t.split("**A4 ")[1].split("**B1")[0]; assert a4.count("*Alt:*")<=3, a4.count("*Alt:*")
print("batches ok", len(rows))
EOF2

checks.name: project.py kickoff --check exists and its selftest passes

evals.name: two-colour-brand-mark-plate-on-a-home-fdm-printer
evals.prompt: Our FDM case has a debossed logo on the face that sits on the print bed and the owner says it looks 'webbed' next to the rest of the face. The printer has an AMS. Fix the logo finish and give me a plate I can print, with the numbers.
evals.expected_output: Names the cause (a bed-face deboss ceiling is a bridge underside beside a glossy bed-contact face) and offers the two first-class options from references/dfm-printed-enclosure.md §8.1 as an owner choice (questionnaire C9): (a) the mark as a top-face feature with the part re-oriented so that face is a top face, plate profile ironing_type top (never topmost), top shell >= recess + 1.0; (b) a flush AMS colour body in the bed layers, mark mirrored in the model, 2 colour layers by default (3 for a light mark), as ONE multi-part object with per-part extruder in the 3MF and one filament JSON per slot carrying filament_colour (the CLI segfaults on a two-filament prime tower without it); never a vertical-wall deboss and never sparse_infill_density 100% (rejected). Adds the FAIL-gated mark rows (recess span <= 6.0, island >= 2.5, colour region >= 0.84, margins >= 1.5, whole-layer depth on the mesh, chirality vs the artwork), a mark coupon first on the plate, and reports per plate minutes, grams per filament, filament changes and the purge share of the mark filament.
assertions: the answer explains the webbing as the bridge-underside ceiling of a bed-face recess, not as a slicer setting

both options are offered as an owner decision: an ironed top-face feature (ironing_type top, not topmost, part re-oriented) and a flush AMS colour body in the bed layers (mirrored, 2 layers default, 3 for a light mark)
the AMS route is one multi-part object with per-part extruder and one filament profile per slot with filament_colour; the agent does not set sparse_infill_density to 100%
FAIL-gated geometry rows with thresholds are listed (recess span, enclosed island, colour-region width, edge margin, whole-layer depth, chirality) and a mark coupon is first on the plate
the plate report states minutes, grams per filament, filament changes and the purge share, and says which check is printer-dependent (the coupon) and which is guaranteed by geometry

evals.name: ee-only-sensor-board-without-a-case
evals.prompt: Spec for a bare 4-layer I2C sensor breakout (USB-C powered, 30 x 20 mm) that ships as a bare PCBA to be plugged into the customer's fixture. No enclosure ever. KiCad + JLCPCB. Set the project up and take it through the gates.
evals.expected_output: Asks A0 first and records scope ee; asks the PCB batches (B1-B8), the bar (D1-D2, not D3), verification (E1, E2, E4, not E3), parts, software, release, identity (not the enclosure batches C1-C9, not the brand-mark question); scaffolds with scripts/project.py scaffold --scope ee so GATES.md has G0 / G1 / G2 / Order (board) / Release and no Case order, M1 or M2 row; project.yaml has no print_targets, case_yaml or mech_record; no case pipeline, census, print DFM, vendor 3D-print quote, coupon or FEA-on-case step is scheduled; the flow is G0 spec round -> G1 schematic (ERC 0) -> G2 layout (DRC 0/0/0, fab DFM mirror 0/0) -> fab DFM on the board and panel -> the owner's order click -> release cut -> production cut keyed on the board md5; the production cut yaml carries no case deliverables.
assertions: A0 scope is asked first and recorded as project.scope: ee plus an owner D row
no enclosure question (C1-C9), design-margin question (D3) or coupon question (E3) is asked; the PCB build questions B1-B8 are asked with recommended answers
docs/governance/GATES.md has G0, G1, G2, Order (board) and Release rows and no Case order, M1 or M2 row; project.yaml has no print_targets, case_yaml or paths.mech_record
no case pipeline, thin-wall census, print-service DFM, coupon, board dummy or case FEA step appears in the plan or the gates
the phase chain named is G0 -> G1 -> G2 -> fab DFM (board and panel) -> order -> release cut -> production cut, all keyed on the board md5
the production cut deliverable list carries no case report, case drawing, STL set or case FEA row
the scaffolded production_cut.yaml carries no OpenSCAD-rendered assembly guide, insert / torque assembly SOP or case manufacturing-spec row

checks.name: ee scaffold: G0 G1 G2 Order(board) Release rows only
checks.run: mkdir -p docs/governance design && cp "$SKILL"/templates/{project.yaml,CLAUDE.md,GATES.md,SPEC.md,STATUS.md,KICKOFF_ANSWERS.md,ENV.md,production_cut.yaml} . && cp "$SKILL"/templates/design/traceability.yaml design/ && "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/project.py scaffold --scope ee project.yaml CLAUDE.md GATES.md SPEC.md STATUS.md KICKOFF_ANSWERS.md ENV.md production_cut.yaml design/traceability.yaml >/dev/null && G=$(grep -o "^| \*\*[A-Za-z0-9 ()]*\*\*" GATES.md | tr -d "*|" | tr -s " \n" " ") && [ "$G" = " G0 G1 G2 Order (board) Release " ]

checks.run: mkdir -p docs/governance design && cp "$SKILL"/templates/{project.yaml,CLAUDE.md,GATES.md,SPEC.md,STATUS.md,KICKOFF_ANSWERS.md,ENV.md,production_cut.yaml} . && cp "$SKILL"/templates/design/traceability.yaml design/ && "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/project.py scaffold --scope ee project.yaml CLAUDE.md GATES.md SPEC.md STATUS.md KICKOFF_ANSWERS.md ENV.md production_cut.yaml design/traceability.yaml >/dev/null && ! grep -q "^print_targets:\|case_yaml:\|mech_record" project.yaml && grep -q "^board:" project.yaml

evals.name: print-kit-entry-point-and-text-gate
evals.prompt: The home-FDM case (tray + body + magnet-held hood + two glued mark plates + dust caps with crush ribs) is ready. Build the print kit for a technician who has never seen the repo and hand it over.
evals.expected_output: One kit folder with a generated START_HERE.md: a print-order table (step / project .3mf name / objects / sliced minutes + grams / check before the next step, coupon gate stated), a numbered assembly sequence (supports out, inserts from the pillar ends body upside down, dry-fit, screws, magnets stack-and-mark + dry attract check THEN CA, plates on the lands, feet LAST), and a report-back table with numeric pass criteria and a named recipient; print sheets named for their .3mf with the Profile line from the 3MF dict; the hardware list and every fastener / material sentence derived from the knobs; the kit text gate run over every emitted text (None / nan / {name}, repo paths, dead file names, snap-tab / screws / PETG tokens under magnets / PLA = FAIL); a watertight row per STL; sidecars drift-checked against the embedded 3MF config; the crush ribs shipped as a bracket plate (0.20 / 0.25 / 0.30, named objects) with an interference-window row, the owner asked to pick after the first print; the hood plate seated on the lands with the bridged strips one layer below and working clearance >= 0.1 as a row.
assertions: START_HERE.md exists at the top of the kit and is generated from kit_facts.json + the sidecars, not typed
the print-order table names the .3mf project files and the print sheets carry the same names
the assembly sequence has magnets dry-fitted with the stack-and-mark rule before any CA and the feet as the last step
the report-back table has a numeric pass criterion per interface and a recipient
a kit text gate fails on None / nan / {name}, repo paths, dead file references and tokens of features the preset disables
the hardware list counts come from the fastener knobs (no typed insert or magnet count)
every exported STL has a watertight row; the sidecar keys a rule depends on are drift-checked against the 3MF config
the ribs ship as a bracket plate with named objects and the owner is asked to choose the value after one print
the glued plate rests on the lands, strip ceilings one layer below, working clearance after EF on both parts >= 0.1 as a row

checks.name: print-kit reference: START_HERE, text gate tokens, magnet sequence, bracket plate
checks.run: grep -q "START_HERE" "$SKILL"/references/print-kit.md && grep -q "{name}" "$SKILL"/references/print-kit.md && grep -q "Dry attract check before any CA" "$SKILL"/references/print-kit.md && grep -q "feet LAST" "$SKILL"/references/print-kit.md && grep -q "bracket plate" "$SKILL"/references/dfm-printed-enclosure.md

evals.name: print-dfm-root-under-rim-flags-and-wall-1-3-passes
evals.prompt: An MJF bracket of record (90 mm long) carries a 2.0 mm rim ring set inboard of its 2.0 mm wall over a lap step so that the rim stands on a 0.5 mm root; the ray census reads >= 2.0 everywhere. The owner wants to upload it to JLC3DP as PA12 (process row jlc_mjf_pa12) and asks whether it is printable; then proposes widening the root to 1.3 mm. Run the print DFM on both and say what each result means.
evals.expected_output: scripts/print_dfm.py --process jlc_mjf_pa12 <stl> on the 0.5-root body: verdict FLAG with rows W wall (wall-class region, median ~0.5-0.7 < wall_min 1.0, extent ~90 mm >= 10 x t) AND R root under a rim / ledge (the same region reads >= 1.0 along the normal) — the ray census cannot see the overlap, the opposing-face tangent ball does; the body is not uploaded (the vendor's checker would pass a root this length up to ~60 mm and its PASS is not sufficient). The 1.3-root body: PASS on every rule (Y INFO lists the 1.0..1.2 band if any). Both records written to out/.../dfm/<piece>.json with the STL md5; the gate line `print_dfm.py --gate` in gates.adopt; the geometry change is a decision row and a generator change, never an edit of the yaml alone; after the vendor's verdict the row goes into docs/quotes/dfm_verdicts.yaml and --validate runs. The pair is scripts/print_dfm.py --selftest's third / fourth case (rim_profile(0.5) vs rim_profile(1.3), 90 mm extrusion) and the smoke's step 0d.
assertions: the 0.5 mm root body is FLAG with both W wall and R root fired and the region's extent ~90 mm, min ~0.5
the agent explains that a normal-ray census misses the root and the opposing-face tangent ball reads it
the 1.3 mm root body is PASS under jlc_mjf_pa12
no upload before the PASS; the vendor's own PASS is called necessary, not sufficient (length-tolerant checker)
the records carry the STL md5 and the gate line joins gates.adopt; the fix is a generator change with a decision row
the vendor's later verdict is appended to dfm_verdicts.yaml and --validate is run; a vendor FLAG on a body we pass would be a RULE DEFECT, not a threshold tweak

checks.name: print_dfm selftest: 0.5 root under a rim FLAGs W + R, 1.3 passes, M manifold, gate enforcement
checks.run: needs-mesh: "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/print_dfm.py --selftest

evals.name: arrival-checklist-before-the-boards-ship
evals.prompt: The rev-0 boards are in production and two blind reviews just merged with 55 findings, 20 of them 'already decided'. The owner says: keep track of everything we must check once the boards are back. Do it.
evals.expected_output: Writes design/arrival_checklist.yaml (sections: before shipment approval from the fab's photos, bench checks in gate order with what each row opens, software gates before the first high-power step with their closing commits, case first article, owner decisions still OPEN with the trigger that resolves each) from the merged reviews' CONFIRMED bench items and the OPEN decision rows, generates docs/production/ARRIVAL_CHECKLIST.md with scripts/arrival_checklist.py, adds the --check line to gates.adopt (project.py gates-required demands it), registers it as a cut deliverable, and marks nothing DONE without evidence; a frozen SPEC's deviations go to docs/spec_sections/SPEC_ERRATA.md as OPEN E-rows, never into SPEC.md.
assertions: the checklist is generated from a yaml (never hand-written markdown) and the --check line is in gates.adopt
every row has id / item / how or trigger / status / evidence; bench rows say what they open and nothing is powered before its row
the ALREADY DECIDED findings are not re-listed as findings; the CONFIRMED bench items become rows
the software gates section names the closing commit per gate
SPEC.md is not edited; deviations are E-rows in SPEC_ERRATA.md marked OPEN
no row is DONE without an evidence cell

checks.name: arrival_checklist selftest (render, counts, DONE needs evidence, status grammar, missing yaml = 2)
checks.run: "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/arrival_checklist.py --selftest

checks.name: the shipped template yaml obeys the script's rules in every scope and the mech scaffold drops the board sections
checks.run: mkdir -p design docs/production && printf 'project: {name: t, scope: mech}\n' > project.yaml && cp "$SKILL"/templates/design/arrival_checklist.yaml design/ && "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/project.py scaffold --scope mech design/arrival_checklist.yaml >/dev/null && sed -i.bak -E 's/\{\{[^{}]*\}\}/X/g' design/arrival_checklist.yaml && "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/arrival_checklist.py >/dev/null && grep -q '^## D\.' docs/production/ARRIVAL_CHECKLIST.md && ! grep -q '^## B\.' docs/production/ARRIVAL_CHECKLIST.md && { "$PY" "$SKILL"/scripts/project.py gates-required || true; } | grep -q arrival_checklist

checks.name: SPEC_ERRATA template ships OPEN rows and SKILL names the rule
checks.run: grep -q 'OPEN (owner)' "$SKILL"/templates/SPEC_ERRATA.md && grep -q 'A frozen SPEC is never edited' "$SKILL"/SKILL.md

evals.name: two-colour-plate-purge-into-infill
evals.prompt: Our AMS plate prints a case body with a second-colour band of accents starting at layer 14 (0.20 mm layers, 20 % gyroid). The owner wants less filament waste. Optimise the plate and show me the numbers.
evals.expected_output: Groups the colour changes into one Z band, turns flush_into_infill (and flush_into_support) on for the body because its colour changes sit above the first sparse-infill layer, calibrates the flush volume for the pair, turns the prime tower off on the single-filament plates, keeps the darker-after-lighter purge out of visible regions (wall_loops >= 3, shells >= 4 over flushed infill), writes every knob into the plate yaml optimise: block and the sidecar, and reports purge grams and tower grams per plate against the SAME plate sliced chute-only (derived from slice_info.config / the M620 count), stating that a 2-layer bed-face colour mark would gain nothing from infill flushing.
assertions: flush_into_infill is enabled only because the colour change sits above the first infill layer, and the agent says a bed-layer mark gains nothing
the purge grams reported are below the chute-only slice of the same plate and both numbers come from the slice report / g-code, not from the yaml
every knob used is in the plate yaml and the sidecar, drift-checked against the embedded 3MF config
the show-through risk is handled (wall loops / shell layers stated, dark-after-light direction kept out of visible regions)
single-filament plates have the prime tower off

checks.name: the optimisation reference carries the flush-into-infill rule with its proof row and the C11 default sets
checks.run: grep -q 'flush_into_infill' "$SKILL"/references/fdm-print-optimisation.md && grep -q 'HAVE sparse infill' "$SKILL"/references/fdm-print-optimisation.md && grep -q 'purge_g' "$SKILL"/references/fdm-print-optimisation.md && grep -q '^## 4. Default knob sets' "$SKILL"/references/fdm-print-optimisation.md && grep -q 'kickoff.enclosure.optimise' "$SKILL"/templates/KICKOFF_ANSWERS.md && grep -q 'optimise:' "$SKILL"/templates/project.yaml
